### 2. First-Principles Computation & Hardware Physical Boundaries

#### 2.1 Exact Memory Breakdown on NVIDIA T4 (Kaggle Free Tier: 15.1 GiB Usable VRAM)
To refute the claim that open-weight deliberative reasoning cannot run on free tiers, we evaluate `DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B` ($N = 7.61 \times 10^9$ parameters) under NF4 quantization:

##### 1. Static Weights ($M_{\text{weights}}$)
* **Linear Layers (4-bit NF4)**: $7.61 \times 10^9 \times 0.5\,\text{bytes} \approx 3.543\,\text{GiB}$
* **Double Quantization Scales** (block size 64, 8-bit secondary scales): $7.61 \times 10^9 \times (1/64) \times 1\,\text{byte} \approx 0.111\,\text{GiB}$
* **Embeddings & LM Head (FP16)** ($V = 152{,}064, d = 3584$): $2 \times 152{,}064 \times 3584 \times 2\,\text{bytes} \approx 0.245\,\text{GiB}$
$$\mathbf{M_{\text{weights}} = 3.543 + 0.111 + 0.245 = 3.899\,\text{GiB} \approx 3.90\,\text{GiB}}$$

##### 2. Dynamic KV Cache ($M_{\text{KV}}$) at Full 32k Sequence Length
For Qwen-2.5-7B architecture: $L = 28$ layers, Grouped Query Attention (GQA) with $n_{\text{kv\_heads}} = 4$, head dimension $d_{\text{head}} = 128$, precision FP16 ($2\,\text{bytes}$), batch size $B = 1$, sequence length $T = 32{,}768$:
$$\text{KV Bytes} = 2 \times L \times n_{\text{kv\_heads}} \times d_{\text{head}} \times T \times b \times B$$
$$\text{KV Bytes} = 2 \times 28 \times 4 \times 128 \times 32{,}768 \times 2 \times 1 = 1{,}879{,}048{,}192\,\text{bytes}$$
$$\mathbf{M_{\text{KV}} = \frac{1{,}879{,}048{,}192}{1024^3} = 1.750\,\text{GiB}}$$

##### 3. Total VRAM Footprint & Safety Margin
Adding CUDA runtime and intermediate activation workspace ($M_{\text{context}} \approx 0.30\,\text{GiB}$):
$$\mathbf{M_{\text{total}} = 3.90\,\text{GiB} + 1.75\,\text{GiB} + 0.30\,\text{GiB} = 5.95\,\text{GiB}}$$
$$\text{Headroom on T4} = 15.10\,\text{GiB} - 5.95\,\text{GiB} = \mathbf{9.15\,\text{GiB}\; (60.6\%\;\text{Free Space})}$$
For students using the smaller `DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B`, total VRAM is $\mathbf{\le 2.2\,\text{GiB}}$, running smoothly on any consumer GPU.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 KAGGLE T4 VRAM BUDGET (DEEPSEEK-R1-7B NF4)                  │
├───────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ NF4 Model Weights                 │ 3.90 GiB                                │
│ 32,768-Token KV Cache (FP16 GQA)  │ 1.75 GiB                                │
│ PyTorch CUDA Runtime & Activation │ 0.30 GiB                                │
│ TOTAL OCCUPIED                    │ 5.95 GiB (< 6 GiB)                      │
│ AVAILABLE HEADROOM ON T4          │ 9.15 GiB (60.6% Free Space)             │
└───────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

#### 2.2 Resolving Thread 3 & 4's `merge_and_unload()` OOM Spike ($18.07\,\text{GiB}$)
In QLoRA fine-tuning, calling `model.merge_and_unload()` on a bitsandbytes 4-bit base model crashes the T4 GPU:
* Unquantized base model weights in FP16: $7.61 \times 10^9 \times 2\,\text{bytes} \approx 14.17\,\text{GiB}$
* 4-bit resident weights still in VRAM: $3.90\,\text{GiB}$
$$\text{Peak Memory} = 14.17\,\text{GiB} + 3.90\,\text{GiB} = \mathbf{18.07\,\text{GiB} > 15.10\,\text{GiB}\; (\text{OOM by } 2.97\,\text{GiB})}$$

##### The Architectural Solution: Host RAM Decoupled Export (`device_map="cpu"`)
Kaggle environments provide **$30.0\,\text{GiB}$ of Host System RAM**. We decouple training from export:
1. **Training (GPU)**: Execute 4-bit QLoRA on the T4 GPU. Save *only* the low-rank adapter weights ($\approx 22\,\text{MB}$).
2. **Export (Host CPU RAM)**: Load the unquantized FP16 base model into Host RAM using `device_map="cpu"`.
$$\text{Peak Host RAM} = 14.17\,\text{GiB} + 0.022\,\text{GiB} \approx 14.2\,\text{GiB} \ll 30.0\,\text{GiB}$$
The merge succeeds with over $15\,\text{GiB}$ of Host RAM to spare, writing sharded safetensors directly to `/kaggle/working` without exceeding the $20\,\text{GB}$ disk quota.

#### 2.3 Exact Binomial Power Math ($N \ge 20, k_{\text{crit}} = 15, \text{Power} = 0.8042$)
Under null hypothesis $H_0: p = 0.50$ (guessing) versus alternative hypothesis $H_1: p_1 = 0.80$ (authentic competence) at $\alpha \le 0.05$ (one-tailed):

1. **Critical Threshold**: For $N = 20$, the rejection region requires $k \ge 15$:
   $$P(X \ge 15 \mid p = 0.50) = \frac{\sum_{j=15}^{20} \binom{20}{j}}{2^{20}} = \frac{21{,}700}{1{,}048{,}576} \approx \mathbf{0.0207} \le 0.05$$
   *(If $k=14$, $P(X \ge 14) \approx 0.0577 > 0.05$, failing significance).*
2. **Statistical Power ($1 - \beta$)**:
   $$\text{Power} = \sum_{j=15}^{20} \binom{20}{j} (0.80)^j (0.20)^{20-j} = \mathbf{0.804207} \approx \mathbf{80.42\%}$$
3. **Power Curve Comparison**:
   * If $N = 7$ (the sample in current Appendix G Section 6): Power collapses to $\mathbf{20.97\%}$.
   * If $N = 10$: Power is $\mathbf{32.22\%}$.
   * If $N = 20$: Power reaches $\mathbf{80.42\%}$.
   This proves that **$N \ge 20$ items is the exact mathematical lower bound** required to avoid a $79\%$ false-negative rate when assessing student mastery.

```python
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
from peft import PeftModel

# 1. 训练阶段仅在 GPU 上保存 LoRA 适配器 (约 22 MB)
# 2. 导出合并阶段解耦至 Kaggle 30 GB 宿主机内存 (device_map="cpu")

    "Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct",
    torch_dtype=torch.float16,
    device_map="cpu",
    low_cpu_mem_usage=True
)
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(base_model, "./lora_adapter")
merged = model.merge_and_unload()
merged.save_pretrained("./dist_qwen_merged", max_shard_size="2GB")
```

### Forensic Engineering Audit: Subtle Edge Cases, Silent Bugs & Mathematical Inconsistencies Across the Repository

**Auditing Standard**: Strictly Proposal-Only (Zero Code/File Modifications)

---

### Category 1: Numerical Instability & Precision Failure Modes

#### 1.1 Attention GEMM FP16 Overflow & Empty Causal Row NaN
* **Location**: [`content/03-attention.js:L90-L150`](file:///D:/CFX%20Modelling/ai-course/content/03-attention.js#L90-L150) & [`content/91-appendix-b-labs.js:L767-L770`](file:///D:/CFX%20Modelling/ai-course/content/91-appendix-b-labs.js#L767-L770)
* **The Obscure Failure Mode**:
  In standard FP16 (IEEE 754 half-precision), the maximum representable finite value is:
  $$\text{FP16}_{\max} = 65{,}504, \quad \text{FP16}_{\min} \approx 6.10 \times 10^{-5}$$
  In Lab E3 ([`91-appendix-b-labs.js:L767`](file:///D:/CFX%20Modelling/ai-course/content/91-appendix-b-labs.js#L767)), attention logits are computed as:
  ```python
  att = (q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * (1.0 / math.sqrt(self.head_dim))
  att = att.masked_fill(self.mask[:, :, :T, :T] == 0, float("-inf"))
  att = F.softmax(att, dim=-1)
  ```
  * **Edge Case A (Dot Product GEMM Overflow)**: In modern 7B/8B models with head dimension $d_k = 128$, activation outliers frequently reach amplitudes of $\pm 50$ to $\pm 100$ in intermediate layers. If `q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)` is executed **before** multiplying by $1/\sqrt{d_k}$, the unscaled dot product sum $\sum_{i=1}^{128} q_i k_i$ easily reaches $100 \times 100 \times 128 = 1{,}280{,}000 \gg 65{,}504$. In FP16, this overflows to `+inf`, causing `inf - inf = NaN` during softmax normalization.
  * **Edge Case B (Mask Overflow & The All-Masked NaN Bug)**: Naive scripts often write `.masked_fill(mask == 0, -1e9)`. In FP16, `-1e9` cannot be represented and underflows to `-inf`. While `exp(-inf) = 0`, if an entire row is masked (e.g., prefix padding tokens or an empty generation prompt), the denominator $\sum_j \exp(z_j) = 0$, producing $\frac{0}{0} = \mathbf{NaN}$.
* **Rigorous Engineering Fix**:
  Scale $Q$ *before* the GEMM: `q = q / math.sqrt(self.head_dim)`, accumulate GEMM in FP32, or use PyTorch's native FlashAttention-2 / SDPA kernel (`F.scaled_dot_product_attention`) which maintains SRAM-level numerically stable online softmax.

---

#### 1.2 RoPE Base Frequency Catastrophe: $\theta = 10{,}000$ vs $500{,}000$
* **Location**: [`content/13-long-context.js:L60-L120`](file:///D:/CFX%20Modelling/ai-course/content/13-long-context.js#L60-L120) & [`content/95-appendix-f-cheatsheet.js:L79`](file:///D:/CFX%20Modelling/ai-course/content/95-appendix-f-cheatsheet.js#L79)
* **The Obscure Failure Mode**:
  RoPE rotary angular frequency for subspace dimension $i \in \{0, \dots, d/2 - 1\}$ is:
  $$\theta_i = b^{-2i/d} \implies \lambda_i = \frac{2\pi}{\theta_i} = 2\pi \cdot b^{2i/d}$$
  * For LLaMA-1/2 ($b = 10{,}000, d = 64$ or $128$):
    $$\lambda_{\max} = 2\pi \cdot 10000^{63/64} \approx 47{,}117 \text{ tokens}$$
  * For LLaMA-3 / Qwen-2.5 ($b = 500{,}000, d = 128$):
    $$\lambda_{\max} = 2\pi \cdot 500000^{63/64} \approx 2\pi \times 408{,}000 \approx \mathbf{2{,}563{,}000 \text{ tokens}}$$
  * **Silent Discrepancy**: If an engineer takes an off-the-shelf fine-tuning script configured for LLaMA-2 (defaulting to `rope_theta = 10000`) and runs it on LLaMA-3 (which expects $500{,}000$), the angular velocities are compressed by a factor of $(500000 / 10000)^{2i/d} \approx \mathbf{50 \times}$ in the low-frequency dimensions. The model's long-range attention weights disperse immediately, causing perplexity to explode beyond $L = 2048$ tokens without throwing any CUDA errors.

### Category 2: Silent Tensor Bugs & Training Inconsistencies

#### 2.1 Causal Mask Static Buffer OOB Crash in Lab E3
* **Location**: [`content/91-appendix-b-labs.js:L758-L768`](file:///D:/CFX%20Modelling/ai-course/content/91-appendix-b-labs.js#L758-L768)
* **The Concrete Bug**:
  In `CausalSelfAttention.__init__`:
  ```python
  self.register_buffer("mask", torch.tril(torch.ones(ctx_len, ctx_len)).view(1, 1, ctx_len, ctx_len))
  ```
  In `forward(x)`:
  ```python
  B, T, C = x.size()
  ...
  att = att.masked_fill(self.mask[:, :, :T, :T] == 0, float("-inf"))
  ```
  * **Failure Mode A (Context Extension Crash)**: If $\text{ctx\_len} = 128$, but an evaluation sequence or extrapolation test inputs $T = 129$ tokens:
    In PyTorch, slicing `self.mask[:, :, :129, :129]` on a tensor of size $128$ does *not* throw an IndexError; it silently returns a tensor of size $(1, 1, 128, 128)$.
    Then `att` has shape $(B, H, 129, 129)$, while the mask has shape $(1, 1, 128, 128)$.
    Execution immediately crashes with:
    `RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (129) must match the size of tensor b (128) at non-singleton dimension 3`!
  * **Failure Mode B (KV-Cache Autoregressive Generation Incompatibility)**: During token-by-token decoding with a KV cache, $T_q = 1$ while $T_k = S$ (past sequence length). Here `att` has shape $(B, H, 1, S)$. Slicing `self.mask[:, :, :1, :1]` yields a $1 \times 1$ mask, failing to broadcast across $S$ key positions.
* **Rigorous Engineering Fix**:
  Do not store a static buffer. Generate the causal mask dynamically or leverage PyTorch SDPA:
  ```python
  # Dynamic causal mask or SDPA
  y = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=(x.size(1) > 1))
  ```

#### 2.2 Gradient Accumulation Micro-Batch Token Imbalance Bug
* **Location**: [`content/05-pretraining.js:L160-L165`](file:///D:/CFX%20Modelling/ai-course/content/05-pretraining.js#L160-L165)
* **The Subtle Mathematical Defect**:
  Section 2.3 asserts: *"因为损失是每个 token 的平均值，而梯度是线性的... 所以通常没问题"*.
  This claim is **mathematically false** whenever micro-batches have variable lengths or padding masks!
  * Suppose $N_{\text{accum}} = 2$.
    * Micro-batch 1 has $N_1 = 1{,}000$ active non-padding tokens.
    * Micro-batch 2 has $N_2 = 200$ active non-padding tokens.
  * Standard naive training loop:
    ```python
    loss = criterion(logits, targets) # reduction='mean'
    loss = loss / accum_steps
    loss.backward()
    ```
  * In micro-batch 1, each token gradient is scaled by $\frac{1}{1000 \times 2} = \frac{1}{2000}$.
  * In micro-batch 2, each token gradient is scaled by $\frac{1}{200 \times 2} = \frac{1}{400}$.
  * **Result**: Tokens in micro-batch 2 are weighted **$5 \times$ higher** than tokens in micro-batch 1!
  * **Exact Mathematical Equality**:
    $$\mathcal{L}_{\text{global}} = \frac{\sum_{m=1}^{M} \sum_{i=1}^{N_m} \ell_{m,i}}{\sum_{m=1}^{M} N_m} \ne \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m=1}^{M} \left( \frac{1}{N_m} \sum_{i=1}^{N_m} \ell_{m,i} \right)$$
  * **Fix**: Use `reduction='sum'` per micro-batch, divided by the total accumulation window token count $\sum N_m$.

---

### Category 3: Tokenizer & Data Pre-Processing Edge Cases

#### 3.1 Streaming Multibyte UTF-8 Boundary Splitting Crash
* **Location**: [`content/02-tokenization.js:L80-L140`](file:///D:/CFX%20Modelling/ai-course/content/02-tokenization.js#L80-L140)
* **The Obscure Failure Mode**:
  UTF-8 encodes Chinese characters using 3 bytes (e.g., `"你"` = `b'\xe4\xbd\xa0'`).
  In byte-level BPE (GPT-4 / Qwen / LLaMA), if a token boundary falls between byte 1 and byte 2 of a multibyte sequence:
  Token $t$ emits `b'\xe4'`, and Token $t+1$ emits `b'\xbd\xa0'`.
  * If a client application naively decodes tokens in a streaming loop:
    ```python
    # Silent crash in production streaming APIs
    for token_id in model.generate_stream(...):
        chunk = tokenizer.decode([token_id]) # or token_bytes.decode('utf-8')
    ```
    Python immediately raises:
    `UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xe4 in position 0: unexpected end of data`!
* **Engineering Fix**:
  Use incremental decoders (`codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')('replace')`) that buffer partial byte sequences until the character completes.

### Category 4: Quantization Edge Cases & Invalidation Proofs

#### 4.1 Unsigned Zero-Point Clipping & True-Zero Destruction
* **Location**: [`content/14-compression.js:L390-L410`](file:///D:/CFX%20Modelling/ai-course/content/14-compression.js#L390-L410)
* **The Formula Audited**:
  $$s = \frac{w_{\max} - w_{\min}}{2^b - 1}, \quad z = \left\lfloor -\frac{w_{\min}}{s} \right\rceil, \quad q = \mathrm{clip}\left(\left\lfloor \frac{w}{s} \right\rceil + z, 0, 2^b - 1\right)$$
* **The Edge Case**:
  If activations or weights are strictly positive (e.g., post-ReLU or SiLU bounded activations where $w_{\min} > 0$):
  $$-\frac{w_{\min}}{s} < 0 \implies z < 0$$
  However, in low-bit hardware runtimes (like `uint8` or `uint4`), the zero-point $z$ must be stored as an **unsigned integer** $z \in [0, 2^b-1]$.
  If $z$ is clamped to $0$, real-world zero ($w = 0.0$) maps to $\hat{w} = s(0 - 0) = 0.0$. BUT if the range $[w_{\min}, w_{\max}]$ does not enclose zero, the true value $0.0$ cannot be represented without rounding error!
  In Transformer causal attention, padding tokens and sparse activations rely on $w = 0.0$ producing exact zeros.
* **Fix**: Force the quantization interval to cover zero:
  $$w_{\min}' = \min(0.0, w_{\min}), \quad w_{\max}' = \max(0.0, w_{\max})$$

---

#### 4.2 AWQ Activation Scaling Non-Commutativity Over Non-Linear Blocks
* **Location**: [`content/14-compression.js:L500-L530`](file:///D:/CFX%20Modelling/ai-course/content/14-compression.js#L500-L530)
* **The Invalidation Proof**:
  AWQ applies channel equivalent transforms:
  $$Y = X W = (X S^{-1}) (S W)$$
  In attention projections ($W_q, W_k, W_v$), $S^{-1}$ is cleanly absorbed into the preceding RMSNorm weight $\gamma$:
  $$\tilde{\gamma}_i = \frac{\gamma_i}{s_i}$$
  **The Edge Case**: What happens in the SwiGLU FFN down-projection ($W_{\text{down}}$)?
  The input to $W_{\text{down}}$ is:
  $$X = \mathrm{SiLU}(X W_{\text{gate}}) \odot (X W_{\text{up}})$$
  Because $\mathrm{SiLU}$ is non-linear:
  $$\mathrm{SiLU}(x \cdot s) \ne \mathrm{SiLU}(x) \cdot s$$
  $S^{-1}$ **cannot** be passed backward through $\mathrm{SiLU}$!
  Therefore, AWQ cannot fuse channel scaling into the gate/up projections without an explicit runtime elementwise de-quantization multiplication, destroying kernel fusion benefits on bandwidth-limited edge GPUs.

### 3. Deep Specification 2: The Rigorous Sign Test Power Threshold ($N \ge 19$)

Section 6 of [`content/96-appendix-g-ai-fluency.js`](file:///D:/CFX%20Modelling/ai-course/content/96-appendix-g-ai-fluency.js#L440-L580) currently uses a toy paired test with $N = 7$ trials (where Prompt B wins 6 and Prompt A wins 1).

#### The Mathematical Proof of Flaw:
Under null hypothesis $H_0: p = 0.5$ (Prompt B is no better than Prompt A):
$$P(K \ge 6 \mid N = 7, p = 0.5) = \binom{7}{6}(0.5)^7 + \binom{7}{7}(0.5)^7 = \frac{7 + 1}{128} = \frac{8}{128} = 0.0625$$
For a **two-tailed test** at standard significance level $\alpha = 0.05$:
$$p\text{-value} = 2 \times 0.0625 = \mathbf{0.125} > 0.05$$
**The result fails to achieve statistical significance.** Even when Prompt B wins nearly all trials ($85.7\%$), $N=7$ is statistically powerless to reject the null hypothesis.

#### The Power Derivation ($N \ge 19$ one-tailed / $N \ge 20$ two-tailed):
To guarantee a test power of $1 - \beta \ge 0.80$ against an alternative hypothesis of genuine prompt superiority ($p_1 = 0.80$) at $\alpha = 0.05$:
* **One-Tailed Test ($\alpha = 0.05$)**:
  * Critical rejection threshold: $k_{\text{crit}} = \min \{ k : \sum_{i=k}^N \binom{N}{i} 0.5^N \le 0.05 \}$.
  * Power: $\sum_{i=k_{\text{crit}}}^N \binom{N}{i} (0.8)^i (0.2)^{N-i}$.
  * For $N = 19$:
    $$\sum_{i=14}^{19} \binom{19}{i} 0.5^{19} = 0.0318 \le 0.05 \implies k_{\text{crit}} = 14$$
    $$\text{Power} = \sum_{i=14}^{19} \binom{19}{i} (0.8)^i (0.2)^{19-i} = \mathbf{0.8144} \ge 0.80$$
    *Thus, $N \ge 19$ is the exact minimal sample size for one-tailed verification.*
* **Two-Tailed Test ($\alpha = 0.05, \alpha/2 = 0.025$)**:
  * For $N = 20$:
    $$\sum_{i=15}^{20} \binom{20}{i} 0.5^{20} = 0.0207 \le 0.025 \implies k_{\text{crit}} = 15$$
    $$\text{Power} = \sum_{i=15}^{20} \binom{20}{i} (0.8)^i (0.2)^{20-i} = \mathbf{0.8042} \ge 0.80$$
    *Thus, $N \ge 20$ is the exact minimal sample size for two-tailed verification.*

#### Concrete Proposed Text Addition for Section 6 in `96-appendix-g-ai-fluency.js`:

```html
<section class="blk blk-m">
  <h4><span class="ic">∑</span>统计推断严肃性警告：样本量法则与功效分析 (Power Analysis)</h4>
  <p>
    <strong>为什么 7 次测试永远无法在 α=0.05 下做出统计拒绝？</strong><br>
    许多工程师用 5 到 7 个样例测试新 Prompt，看到“赢了 6 次”就认为通过了验证。
    在双尾检验中，即便 7 次赢 6 次，其零假设概率 \(p = 2 \times \frac{7+1}{128} = 0.125 > 0.05\)，在统计学上<strong>完全无法排除随机巧合</strong>。
  </p>
  <p>
    根据二项检验功效分析（设定第一类错误率 \(\alpha = 0.05\)，真有效率目标 \(p_1 = 0.80\)，统计功效目标 \(1 - \beta \ge 0.80\)）：
  </p>
  <ul>
    <li><strong>单尾检验绝对下限</strong>：\(N \ge 19\)，拒绝临界值 \(k_{\text{crit}} = 14\)（功效达到 81.44%）；</li>
    <li><strong>双尾检验严谨标准</strong>：\(N \ge 20\)，拒绝临界值 \(k_{\text{crit}} = 15\)（功效达到 80.42%）。</li>
  </ul>
  <p>
    <strong>工程守则</strong>：任何声称“新 Prompt / 新模型版本在生产中显著提升”的技术报告，
    若配对评估样本量 \(N < 19\)，一律视为“主观工程臆测”，不得签发上线变更批准。
    这正是模块 09 中标准误差下限 \(\mathrm{SE} = \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{N}}\) 在微调与提示词评估中的直接贯彻。
  </p>
</section>
```

# Thread 9 — Socratic Devil's Advocate: Is This a `Crash Course`?

**Verdict: No. For a ChatGPT-web-box + basic Python beginner, this is deceptive marketing.**

I stepped into the shoes. I verified with my own eyes. I launched 4 subagents, one per file. I sparingly consulted GPT-6.1-Sol Light via `delegate_task` (`codex/gpt-6.1-sol`, `reasoningEffort:low`, `taskId: bench-gpt61sol-001` — still `working` at synthesis time, so I do not fabricate its output).

What I *did* verify directly:

* `01-language-models.js:14` promises: `这一讲全程用日常话和比喻，不写代码，不推公式。`
* `01-language-models.js:17-19` — **3 lines later** — graded quiz: `z1=0,z2=0`, `Softmax`, `L=-ln p1`, answer `0.693`, `data-tol=0.01`.
* `06-parallelism.js:8` promises: `minutes:40`, `06-parallelism.js:17-23` promises `零基础入口`, stone-lifting analogy.
* `06-parallelism.js:50-63` — 10 lines later: `Comm_DP≈2N`, `Comm_TP≈2L·B·S·d`, `bubble≈(p-1)/(m+p-1)`, `L=32, B·S=10^4, d=4096`.

That pattern — friendly wrapper, hostile core — repeats in all 4 files. `POLISH-CONTRACT.md` makes it unfixable by polish alone: formulas, numbers, code, `h3` count are all frozen. You cannot language-polish a structural cliff.

## 1. The Four Vertical Cliffs

### Cliff 0→1: `01-language-models.js` (267 lines, 19 formulas, 0 runnable blocks)

Persona has: `print/for/import math`. Needs on line 17: `log-prob, ln vs log2, logits z, one-hot y, softmax, cross-entropy, nats`.

1. **L17-28 Quiz-before-teaching:** Must output `ln2≈0.693` before `Softmax` is defined. First interaction = failure = "I don't belong."
2. **L108-126 Magic 0.69 / 0.33 / 0:** `ln` never defined. Why does 50/50 = 0.69 not 0.5? No `python -math.log(0.5)` bridge.
3. **L188-205 Paper-gradient wall:** 10 formulas in one accordion: `e^2.0≈7.389`, `L=-sum y_i ln p_i`, `∂L/∂z1=p1-y1=-0.269`, `z←z-η∇L`, `单纯形守恒`. Leap from `只看分差` intuition to vector calculus + `η, ∇, ∂`.

> Deception: `minutes:35`, `折叠块第二遍看，第一遍跳过不影响连贯` — false. The graded math on L17 can't be skipped.

### Cliff 2: `02-tokenization.js` (650 lines, ~30 `<code>`, 0 runnable Python)

Promise L13: `只讲直觉和取舍，不贴完整代码` — true, and that's the problem.

1. **L67-110 Unicode/bytes:** `len("你")==1` mental model shattered. `256字节→上百万编号`, `汉字3字节表情4字节`, `256映射表` — assumed to explain Chinese 2-4x price later.
2. **L115-122,166-182 + 524-557 BPE counting:** Weighted counting `26=2+6+18`, tie-break `按字典序`, order-matters `按学到先后`, info `词表翻倍多1份信息/5-6%`, plus `O(T^2)`, `(6-4)/6≈33.3%`. Beginner cannot hand-verify 26 without error. Feels like stupidity, not missing prereq.
3. **L222-223,231-339 Invisible regex + math:** `片段边界由一条正则决定。竖线是从左到右的或` — pattern never shown. Must memorize 5 magic splits (`123→123/456/789/0`, `I'm→I/'m/ not`) + `前瞻只吃前一个空格` on faith. Then immediately `fertility`, `cost=tokens/1M*单价`, `3x→9x compute`, `2^80`, `1024=2^10`.

### B. Loss reduction — mean vs sum (silent correctness bug)

# Thread 10: Curriculum Synthesis & Tiered Multi-Track Architecture

> Read-only debate contribution. No files modified.
> Inspected: `ai-course/README.md`, `STYLE-CONTRACT.md`, `content/00-orientation.js`, `content/95-appendix-f-cheatsheet.js` + `content/` listing. Three parallel subagent evaluations launched for Track A / B / C. `GPT-6.1-Sol` not consulted — taxonomy question was answerable from in-repo evidence, so per sparing-use rule no external call was made.

## 1. Diagnosis: why this course both succeeds and overwhelms

Strengths are real and must not be diluted:

* **Rigorous math with checkable numbers:** `Attn=softmax(QK^T/sqrt(dk)+M)V`, `N≈12Ld^2+|V|d`, `M_train≈16N+act`, `C≈6ND`, DPO/GRPO losses, ridge/LOOCV/VC in Ch.09 — all with hand-calcs.
* **Real empirical anchors:** Llama-3-8B audit in `appF §2.1` (41.9M attn / 176.2M SwiGLU / 8.03B total, explains 1.06B gap vs rule), 7B→112GB impossibility proof, QLoRA r=16 13.6M/41.9M, KV 8k≈1GiB, `GPU-hours=C/(peak·MFU·3600)`.
* **Failure-mode tables:** `appF §8` + per-chapter `blk-warn` (symptom→cause→one-line verification→fix), enforced by `STYLE-CONTRACT §4`.
* **Offline accessibility + handbook design:** KaTeX bundled, `appF` 11-section cheatsheet, per-lecture mini-TOC, `/` search, `acc` folds, print-to-PDF.

Overwhelm source is structural, not content:

* README says "24 modules / 6-12h", `00-orientation.js §3/§7` says `00→P→01…29` + 12-week ending at Ch.16, actual ship is **38 files: 00,00b,01-29,90-96 (A–G), 36 modules, 1000s formulas, 145 quizzes**. Novice sees 36/36 progress and stalls.
* Linear order `00→P→01…` buries the practitioner path and the handbook path. Default rendering shows everything; `acc[data-badge="可选/动笔/进阶…"]` has no consistent "safe to skip vs must do" signal across tracks.
* `STYLE-CONTRACT §3` depth floor (3 hand-calcs, 2 tables, `blk-lab` 30-min impl, `h3≥7`, `blk-eco`) correctly protects Ch.17-24 from outline-drift — but without tier markers novices try to satisfy it all at once.

**Synthesis thesis:** don't simplify content. Add a **thin overlay routing layer** — three explicit tracks + shared Appendix F hub — with zero edits to existing chapters (complies with `STYLE-CONTRACT §0` iron law #1/#4).

## 2. Proposed three-track architecture

All three share `appF` as graduation/handbook. Default chapter rendering unchanged.

### Track A: 3-Day LLM Mental Model (~6h, novice)

Principle: read named sections only; all `acc` deep-dives deferred.

| Day | Modules (core sections only) | Intuition gained |
|---|---|---|
| **D1 ~115m** | `m0 §§1,4` (10m) + `mP §0,§5,§7` (40m) + `m1 §§1,3,4` + 1 softmax+CE calc (35m) + `appF §1 rows 1-4` (15m) | next-token, CE, PPL, temperature |
| **D2 ~120m** | `m2 §§1,4,6,7.1,8` (30m) + `m3 §§1,2(one calc),3,7.5` (45m) + `m4 §§1,2,4` (30m) + `appF §1 rows 5-7 + §2 rows 1-5` (15m) | tokens/fertility, attention as weighted average, causal mask, `12Ld²` / `16N` / KV bytes |
| **D3 ~120m** | `m8 §§1-3,5,6` (35m) + `m14 §0-1` (20m) + `m5 §6` + `m7 §1` excerpts (20m) + `appF §§2,5,6,7,8` + drill (30m) | sampling, quant `s=(wmax-wmin)/(2^b-1)`, `C≈6ND`, SFT-vs-RAG decision, handbook habit |

~7 IDs: `m0,mP,m1,m2,m3,m4,m8` + excerpts + `appF`. Explicit DEFER with re-entry: FSDP/TP (`m06`)→return at T4×2; GRPO/PPO→only if verifiable; MoE/RoPE-extrap/serving/distill/RAG/agents/safety/architectures/consciousness→Track B/C via `appF §11` one-liners.

### Track B: 4-Week Kaggle T4 Practitioner (coder, lab-first)

Principle: `blk-lab` + failure table + `appF` table first; `blk-m` derivations black-boxed as `[TRUST → F§N]`. All on single T4 16GB.

| Wk | Lab-first | Desk tables | Deliverable |
|---|---|---|---|
| **W1 budget+smoke** | B-E3 mini-Transformer + B-E2 fertility + `00 §6` env check | F§2口诀, F§6 (16GB: scratch≤300M, QLoRA≤7B-short), F§7 commands | loss curve + `peak_vram calc vs measured` + tok/s |

### Track C: 12-Week First-Principles Master (researcher, uncompromised)

Preserves `00 §7` 6-8h/wk cadence; adds proof obligation, not chapters. Load-bearing spine: `P→01→03→04→05→07→09`.

W1 P+01+02 (softmax/CE grad, BPE) → W2 03+04 (variance proof, RoPE group `R_m^T R_n=R_{n-m}`, Llama audit gate) → W3 05+10 (Chinchilla Lagrange `D≈20N` + `6ND`→GPU-h, state when to violate for inference-optimal) → W4 06+28 (FSDP/TP/SPMD) → W5 07 SFT/LoRA/DPO (`Z(x)` cancellation + single-step calc) → W6 07 GRPO + 08 + 17 (group advantage, `1-(1-p)^n`, quant step) → **W7 09+E7 double-week capstone methods** (grouped split, ladder, `SE`, permutation, ridge/`df(λ)`/LOOCV/VC-vacuous) → W8 10+11+23 (Roofline, contamination) → W9 12+13+03-backlink (YaRN, MoE) → W10 14+15+16 (GPTQ-OBS, prefix-cache, distill `αCE+(1-α)T²KL`) → W11 18+19+20+21 (RAG/agent/safety/SSM+InfoNCE) → W12 29+22+F§9 CP1-8 (report + consciousness-as-methods-seminar).

Compare E4's own expected log (`91:1352-1355`: 1.84→0.18 in 30 steps on 3 unique samples) — on 2 unique samples collapse is steeper and `rewards/margins` (E5) cannot be defined. Violates `09` grouped-split/ladder and `appF §4` (LoRA needs diverse `messages`, assistant-only loss).

## Thread 10 — Deliberated synthesis (Round 2 + rigor mandate)

### 0. What changed vs my 18-second judgments

Prior claim "E4 3-sample = authentic, M28 2-sample = toy" was **numerology**. Both are memorization regime:

* E4: 30 steps × eff.batch 16 = 480 visits / 3 uniques = **160 epochs/sample**, ~450 unique tokens vs 18.46M trainable = **41,000 params/token**. Loss 1.84→0.18 in 25 steps is hash-table collapse. Worse, E4's "inference check" reuses training sample #3 verbatim (`91:1317-1334` vs `:1357-1359`).
* M28: 2 uniques ×40/50 (itself inconsistent: `28:97` says ×50, `28:175` says ×40), `r=8 q/v-only` 1.09M/0.07% — weakest config per `07:77-78`.

So the honest ladder is: **M28 = run-through stub, E4 = validated stub with machine-checkable gates, neither = generalizable SFT**. Track B must say so in `00c`.

### 1. Rigorous recomputation (my own, not subagent hand-wave)

Qwen2.5-1.5B (`91:1102-1105`: N=1,543,714,816, d=1536, L=28, d_ffn=8960, V=151936; `28:232-241`: kv_heads=2, head_dim=128 → kv_dim=256):

| proj | W0 | r16 `r(d+k)` |
|---|---|---|
| q/o `1536×1536` | 49,152 each |
| k/v `256×1536` | 28,672 each |
| gate/up `8960×1536`, down `1536×8960` | 167,936 each |

Per-layer 659,456 (attn 155,648 + MLP 503,808 — MLP is 76% of capacity) ×28 = **18,464,768 ≈ 1.196% of base / 1.18% of PEFT total** — matches `91:1349,1369` within counting noise. M28 q/v-only r8: 38,912/layer ×28 = **1,089,536 / 0.071%** — 17× smaller. Naive `12Ld²+Vd`=1.03B undercounts Qwen by 517M because `d_ffn=8960≫8d/3` — same GQA lesson as `F§2.1` Llama audit.

VRAM (MiB): fp16 base 2944.4, NF4-4.127bit 759.5, LoRA w+g 70.4, opt-8bit 105.6 (fp32-equiv 211.3), act B=2/s=512 ckpt-on 350, noise 650 → **1935.6 MiB = 1.890 GiB** ✓ (`91:1127`). T4-16GB = **14.90 GiB** usable, so 1.89 GiB = 12% — but best-case only:

* B=2/s=4096 ckpt-linear: act 2800MB → peak **4.28 GiB**; eager `O(s²)`: 22,400MB → OOM.
* B=4/s=4096: 7.02 GiB linear, 44.8GB eager → OOM.
* B=2/s=10k ("万级上下文" `91:1138`): 8.22 GiB linear even before fragmentation/dequant scratch.
* `27-hardware:215` already warns "batch×seq涨8倍即爆" — E4's table needs an `s`-scaling footnote; `00c` must pin each VRAM row to its `(B,s,ckpt,optim)` tuple, never rescale.

Merge RAM: 2× fp16 1.5B = **5.75GB** + tokenizer — fits Kaggle 30GB host (`29:58-60` `device_map="cpu"`) ✓. But `29:89,106` `FROM ./safetensors-dir / ollama reads safetensors` is false — Ollama needs `FROM ./model.gguf`. And 4-bit base cannot `merge_and_unload` in place (`91:1390`): must reload fp16 base + `PeftModel.from_pretrained(...).merge`.

Power: SE=2.4/√N → N=2:1.70, N=3:1.39, N=19:0.55 (2SE=1.10), N=250:0.15 (2SE=0.30 ✓ `09:99-107`). N=19 @ d=0.5 → δ=1.54 → power ≈32%, not 80% (needs ~63/arm). With artist-grouping ICC≈0.3/m=12.5: DEFF=4.45, N_eff(250)=56, **SE_eff=0.32 not 0.15** — `09`'s "0.30s≈2SE p≈0.05" flips to 0.94SE p≈0.35. So N≥19 is an **entry gate**, never a significance license; Track B W3 must require GroupKFold + permutation B≥200 + preregistered RMSE + effect size, else only conclusion permitted is "cannot reject null."

Pacing (antithesis wins): E4 30–60min + installs 10–20 + CPU merge 10–15 + Ollama/GGUF debug 15–30 + schema-gate 20–40 = **85–165min**. `00c` must budget W4 as 2 sessions, not "30min smoke."

```python
  "content/00c-tracks.js",   # PROPOSED ADD — router; nothing else in this list moves
  # Part 1: 底座原理
  "content/01-language-models.js",
```

Then `python tools/bundle_content.py` rebuilds `assets/course-bundle.js`. Dev servers serving `content/` directly need no change (file auto-loads alphabetically in validator order).

### 3. How progress avoids corrupting existing state

* Active-track switch writes only `tracks:active`; per-track "7/7" counters read `tracks:done:<id>` filtered to that track's `moduleRefs`, while the existing `progNum x/y` (`:1326-1327`) keeps counting full `done[]` — both visible, neither overwrites the other.
* Gate evidence (N, RMSE±SD, p, d, dispatch log) lives under `tracks:gates/dispatches`, exported inside the same `llm-crash-course-progress.json` envelope as new sibling keys — `PROG.push/merge` ignores unknown keys today, so a future additive `merge` clause for `tracks` is proposed separately, never by editing current merge lines.

This makes `00c` a pure router + gates + schema registry: three doors, one handbook hub, full depth preserved behind labeled return paths.

## Forensic edge-case audit (all read directly, proposal-only)

### A. Numerical instability

**A1. fp16 softmax exp-overflow — `03-attention.js:106-114`, `91:767-769`, cheatsheet `95:33`.**
Unscaled dot std is `√d_k` (`03:100-102`); d=128 → std 11.3, tails 30–40. `exp(11)=59,874` vs fp16 max 65,504 — margin 9%. My recomputation confirms overflow at `z≈11.09`. Course states subtract-max obliquely (`95:33` 誤用列 "忘了先减去最大值") but E3 kernel (`91:767-769`: `(q@k)*scale → masked_fill(-inf) → F.softmax`) shows no explicit `z-max` and no autocast-upcast note. On T4 fp16 autocast the pre-softmax lives in fp16; one outlier head → `inf → NaN` loss (`05:22` row lists NaN but blames LR only). *Proposed router guard:* Track B smoke asserts `loss!=NaN` (`91:1149`) already; add `00c` gate note: "softmax must run in fp32 (autocast upcast) even when GEMM is fp16; verify by `att.dtype` after `masked_fill`."

**A2. RoPE base 10k vs 500k silent 44× error — `13-long-context.js:69-113` vs `95:79`.**
Hand calc pins `b=10000,d=64`: `θ31≈1.334e-4, λ31≈47,117` (`13:112-113`, quiz `:207-215`). But `F§2.1` Llama-3 config is `rope_theta=5×10⁵` (`95:79`). Recomputed: b=500k → `θ31≈3.01e-6, λ31≈2,084,765` — **44× larger**. `13:71` scopes `b=10000` to "LLaMA-1/2" yet nothing warns that YaRN thresholds `α=1,β=32` (`13:156-162`, `21:464-466`) and `√(1/t)` temp fix (`13:172`) were tuned for 10k. Copying the 47k number onto a 500k model (Qwen2.5 theta undisclosed in M28/E4) misplaces every low-freq decision by >order of magnitude. *Proposed guard:* `00c` prereq edge `m13→m3` carries `b` as parameter; E-worksheet must print `b` before any λ.

**A3. RMSNorm ε-NaN — `04:277,315`.**
Table `:315` admits "删掉ε会出现NaN" but no value pinned. bf16 epsilon `1e-6` underflows variance floor on near-zero residual early in training. *Guard:* assert `eps≥1e-6 (bf16) / 1e-8 (fp32)` in smoke.

### B. Silent tensor bugs

**B1. Causal-mask slicing correct but truncation-brittle — `91:758,768,814-815`, `91:1067-1068`.**
`register_buffer(tril(ones(ctx,ctx)).view(1,1,ctx,ctx))` + `mask[:,:,:T,:T]==0 → -inf` is correct for `T≤ctx`. Failure is silent at generate: `pos=arange(0,T)` (`91:814`) + `wpe(pos)` overflows at `T=ctx+1` → `IndexError` unless caller slices `idx[:,-ctx:]` (`91:1067-1068` documents, but no assert in generate loop). Off-by-one variant: slicing `[:-1]` vs Learned `wpe` shifts every RoPE/absolute position by one — loss still drops (model learns shifted LM) but E7 ladder compares shifted vs unshifted unfairly. *Guard:* Track B W1 gate: `assert T<=ctx_len` + `idx[:,-ctx_len:]` wrapper test.

**B2. `triu` vs `tril` silent inversion — `91:1078-1080`.**
Documented ("写成`triu`只能看到未来"), but the failure signature ("loss≈log(V)≈4.57") is indistinguishable from bad-LR. Router should order the check first (mask direction before LR sweep).

**B3. Loss `mean` vs token-weighted sum under grad-accum + packing — `91:822-823`, `91:1725`, `28:115,190`, `91:1289,1512`.**
`F.cross_entropy(...view(-1))` defaults `mean`; JAX `jnp.mean(loss)` (`91:1725`) same. With `batch=4,accum=2` (M28) vs `batch=2,accum=8` (E4), per-micro mean gives a 10-token and a 510-token micro-batch **equal weight** (51× distortion vs token-weighting). Add packing (`90:49` warns needs block-diagonal mask; `07:58` mentions packing) + `max_seq_length=512` truncation (`28:119,203`, `91:1306`): truncated assistant tails vanish from loss silently, short samples dominate. M28 additionally trains on `dataset_text_field="text"` with **no completion mask** — prompt tokens earn loss, contradicting its own `07:50` formula `-1/|y|Σ_{t∈y}` and E4's `labels==-100` gate (`91:1147,1161`). *Guard (already in E4, must be gate):* fail W2 without `labels==-100` proof + truncation counter (`n_truncated` logged).

**B4. `view` vs `contiguous` — `91:763-771,1075-1077`, `03:292-299` table.**
`transpose(1,2)` → non-contiguous; `view` before `.contiguous()` throws (`91:1075`), but the table at `03:297` documents it while E3 code at `91:771` does it right (`transpose.contiguous.view`) — learner copying fragments in wrong order hits the error. *Guard:* keep as first-fix checklist item.

**B5. `history.append(loss)` graph leak — `91:1083-1084`.**
Saves full autograd graph per step → linear VRAM growth misdiagnosed as fragmentation. `loss.item()` gate already documented; promote to W1 smoke assert.

### C. Tokenizer & data

**C1. Fertility `tok/char` incomparable across scripts — `91:536-545,592-601`.**
`n_chars=len(text)` counts codepoints; recomputed: 15-Hanzi sample = 45 UTF-8 bytes (3.0 B/char), emoji `👨‍👩‍👧` len=5 chars/18 bytes. `fertility=n_tok/n_chars` mixes 1B/char English with 3B/char Chinese; `bytes/token` partially corrects but the "本土词表3×" conclusion (`91:561`) is script-dependent. Empty-string edge: `n_chars=0` → ZeroDivision (no guard). *Guard:* report `tok/byte` alongside, never `tok/char` alone for CJK.

**C2. `Qwen.encode` vs `tiktoken.encode` off-by-specials — `91:581-590`.**
`tiktoken.encode` adds no specials; `AutoTokenizer.encode(t)` defaults `add_special_tokens=True` (1–2 extra `<|im_start|>` etc.). Fertility table compares shifted counts. *Guard:* pass `add_special_tokens=False` for measurement.

**C3. `padding_side` flip-flop — `91:1160,1252,1378,1435,1488,1576-1577`.**
E4 trains `right` (`:1252`), E5/DPO **requires** `left` (`:1435,1488`, error `:1576`). Reusing the same tokenizer object E4→E5 without reset silently misaligns batch RoPE positions (right-padded batch decodes position ids include pad slots). E5 code does reset — but M28 never sets it at all. *Guard:* W2→W3 handoff asserts `padding_side` value in log.

**C4. `pad_to_multiple_of=8/16` (`91:131`) vs DPO left-pad interaction.**
Right-pad + multiple-of-8 changes effective `T` per batch → KV/act ledger (`B=2,s=512`) drifts ±8. Trivial alone, compounds with B1/B3 at s=4096.

### D. Quantization

**D1. NF4 4.127 bits, not 4.0 — `91:1111-1112`, `14:773-781`.**
Double-quant overhead makes `0.531 B/param`, 3.76× not 4.0× (`14:781`). Learners budgeting "4-bit = quarter" under-provision by 6% + unquantized embed/norm/head (`14:987-989`: only Linear quantized). *Guard:* vramRows carry measured config tuples (done in `00c` schema).

**D2. AWQ outlier-protection vs BNB-NF4 conflation — `14:932,976-977`.**
`:932` prescribes "离群通道保留fp16 / AWQ按激活幅度保护" while E4/E8 run BNB-NF4 which has **no activation-aware scaling** — outliers clip through the same `s=(wmax-wmin)/(2^b-1)` grid (`F§1`). `14:982-984` delta 0.1–0.5 vs torchao 0.63 example shows the gap, but no gate stops a learner applying NF4 perplexity conclusions to AWQ (zero-point clipping differs: symmetric-NF4 vs asymmetric-group-zero). Long-tail delta 2.0-vs-0.2 split (`14:992-994`) is the detector. *Guard:* W4 must report full + tail delta separately.

**D3. KV-quant forgotten — `14:942`, `08:349`.**
Weight-only int4 halves weights but KV stays fp16 and grows linearly (`08:295-297`); 10×8K fp16 KV = 10.6GB (`14:1027-1029`) erases the vint4 win at batch. E8 ledger must include KV line.

### E. Code & lab (P0s)

**E1. E4 Step 7 merges a 4-bit base in place — `91:1261-1266` (NF4 load) → `:1337` `model.merge_and_unload()`.**
Directly contradicts its own error entry `:1390-1391` (`Cannot merge LORA when base in 4-bit → reload fp16 base + PeftModel.from_pretrained.merge`). On current peft this throws; on older it silently dequantizes layer-by-layer with 3GB transient (unbudgeted in 1.89 GiB ledger). M29's CPU path (`29:57-72`) is the correct pattern. *Proposed gate (no file edit):* W4 requires fp16-base reload proof + `merged config.json + safetensors` listing (`91:1368-1372` record row).

**E2. M29 Ollama target is not loadable — `29:89-106`.**
`FROM ./qwen2.5-crossfade-merged` (safetensors dir) + claim "Ollama自动读safetensors" (`29:106`) is false; `ollama create` needs `FROM ./model.gguf`. Every student bricks step 1. Plus `:132-141` POST has no timeout/try, `stream:False` but no `temperature/top_p` passthrough (Modelfile `:92-93` temp ignored), `:141` returns raw string, `:145-147` prints it as "Autonomous Parameter Generation" (`29:121-123`) with the `100%准度/<200ms` claim (`29:172-173`) on N=2 (SE=1.70s — vacuous). *Guard:* W4 dispatch schema + GGUF-hash + latency log (in `00c` gates, not a chapter edit).

**E3. Unpinned `!pip install -q transformers peft trl accelerate bitsandbytes datasets` — `28:54`, `91:1186,1453`.**
TRL broke `SFTTrainer(dataset_text_field="messages")` (`91:1305`) vs `"text"` (`28:119`) across versions; `completion_only_loss/packing` (`92:1359`) renamed twice; `bitsandbytes` CUDA-wheel vs CPU fallback (`14:976-977` torchao note). Repro from 3 months ago fails differently today. `92:1641,1646` already prescribes `pip show trl` version lock — promote to W1 log line (`transformers/peft/trl/bitsandbytes` versions + `torch.cuda` build).

**E4. `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` set too late / never — `91:1200` vs M28 (absent).**
E4 sets env **after** `import torch` (`91:1188`) but before first CUDA call (`91:1203-1205`) — works by luck; any earlier `torch.cuda` probe (copy-pasted snippet order) silently ignores it, fragmentation OOM returns (`91:1392-1393` fix looks "broken"). M28 full script sets nothing. Plus no `torch.cuda.empty_cache()/ipc_collect` + `save_strategy="no"` means `/kaggle/working` fills with `qwen_lora_out` checkpoints on retry → disk-full crash (Kaggle ~20GB) misread as OOM. *Guard:* env-first-cell assert + `df -h /kaggle/working` in smoke.

**E5. E5 DPO memory ledger omits reference-model path — `91:1415-1426`.**
`ref_model=None` + `disable_adapter` still runs **two forwards** (chosen+rejected → eff. 2B=4, act 600MB `:1419-1421`) plus `torch.gather` 40MB — but grad flows only through LoRA; base grad checkpointing (`use_reentrant:False`, `use_cache=False` `:1388-1389`) must hold for **both** passes or step-0 hang returns. Single-pass smoke (`:1436`: 1 pair finite logps; `:1437`: 10 steps from 0.693) is the correct detector — keep as W3 entry gate.

All above are router/checklist/validator-note proposals. Core thesis stands; these are the teeth that make Track B gates enforceable.

```js
if (typeof window !== 'undefined') {
  window.TRACKS_ROUTER = {
    version: 1,
    activeDefault: 'full',
    tracks: {
      'track-a': { short: 'a', modules: ['m0', 'mP', 'm1', 'm2', 'm3', 'm4', 'm8', 'appF'] },
      'track-b': { short: 'b', modules: ['m28', 'm29', 'appB', 'appF', 'm9', 'm7'], labs: ['E3', 'E4', 'E7', 'E5', 'E8'] },
      'track-c': { short: 'c', spine: ['mP', 'm1', 'm3', 'm4', 'm5', 'm7', 'm9'] },
      'full': { short: 'full', modules: [] }
    },
    badges: { allow: ['ke-xuan', 'dong-bi', 'jin-jie'], pillClass: 'pill' },
    keys: { active: 'tracks:active', donePrefix: 'tracks:done:', gates: 'tracks:gates', dispatches: 'tracks:dispatches' },
    prereq: { spine: ['mP', 'm1', 'm3', 'm4', 'm5', 'm7', 'm9'] }
  };
}

(function tracksRouterRuntime() {
  if (typeof document === 'undefined') { return; }
  if (typeof location === 'undefined') { return; }
  function lsGet(k, d) {
    try {
      var v = null;
      try { v = localStorage.getItem('llmcourse:' + k); } catch (e) { v = null; }
      return v === null ? d : JSON.parse(v);
    } catch (e) { return d; }
  }
  function lsSet(k, v) {
    try { localStorage.setItem('llmcourse:' + k, JSON.stringify(v)); } catch (e) {}
  }
  function shortOf(t) {
    if (t === 'a' || t === 'track-a') { return 'track-a'; }
    if (t === 'b' || t === 'track-b') { return 'track-b'; }
    if (t === 'c' || t === 'track-c') { return 'track-c'; }
    return 'full';
  }
  function parseTrack() {
    var q = null;
    try { q = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('track'); } catch (e) { q = null; }
    if (q) { return shortOf(q); }
    var saved = lsGet('tracks:active', 'full');
    return shortOf(saved);
  }
  function membersOf(track) {
    try {
      var r = window.TRACKS_ROUTER.tracks[track];
      return (r && r.modules) || [];
    } catch (e) { return []; }
  }
  function applyFilter(track) {
    var members = membersOf(track);
    var links = [];
    try { links = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('#nav a[data-id]')); } catch (e) { links = []; }
    var i = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < links.length; i = i + 1) {
      var el = links[i];
      var id = null;
      try { id = el.getAttribute('data-id'); } catch (e) { id = null; }
      if (track === 'full' || !members.length) {
        try { el.hidden = false; } catch (e) {}
      } else {
        var keep = members.indexOf(id) >= 0 || id === 'm0c';
        try { el.hidden = !keep; } catch (e) {}
      }
    }
    paintPills(track, members);
  }
  function pillText(track, id) {
    if (track === 'track-a') { return 'A-core'; }
    if (track === 'track-b') {
      if (id === 'appB' || id === 'm28' || id === 'm29') { return 'B-lab'; }
      return 'B-ref';
    }
    if (track === 'track-c') { return 'C-spine'; }
    return '';
  }
  function paintPills(track, members) {
    if (track === 'full') { return; }
    var i = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < members.length; i = i + 1) {
      var id = members[i];
      var sec = null;
      try { sec = document.getElementById(id); } catch (e) { sec = null; }
      if (!sec) { continue; }
      var head = null;
      try { head = sec.querySelector('.mod-head'); } catch (e) { head = null; }
      if (!head) { continue; }
      var dup = null;
      try { dup = head.querySelector('[data-track-pill]'); } catch (e) { dup = null; }
      if (dup) { continue; }
      var s = null;
      try {
        s = document.createElement('span');
        s.className = 'pill';
        s.setAttribute('data-track-pill', track);
        s.textContent = pillText(track, id);
        head.appendChild(s);
      } catch (e) {}
    }
  }
  function paintCounts() {
    var done = lsGet('progress', null);
    var arr = [];
    try { arr = (done && done.done) || []; } catch (e) { arr = []; }
    var keys = ['track-a', 'track-b', 'track-c'];
    var k = 0;
    for (k = 0; k < keys.length; k = k + 1) {
      var t = keys[k];
      var members = membersOf(t);
      var n = 0;
      var j = 0;
      for (j = 0; j < members.length; j = j + 1) {
        if (arr.indexOf(members[j]) >= 0) { n = n + 1; }
      }
      var nodes = [];
      try { nodes = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('[data-track-count="' + t + '"]')); } catch (e) { nodes = []; }
      var m = 0;
      for (m = 0; m < nodes.length; m = m + 1) {
        try { nodes[m].textContent = n + '/' + members.length; } catch (e) {}
      }
    }
  }
  function wireLinks() {
    var nodes = [];
    try { nodes = Array.prototype.slice.call(document.querySelectorAll('a[href^="?track="]')); } catch (e) { nodes = []; }
    var i = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < nodes.length; i = i + 1) {
      (function (a) {
        try {
          if (a.getAttribute('data-track-wired')) { return; }
          a.setAttribute('data-track-wired', '1');
          a.addEventListener('click', function (ev) {
            var href = ' ';
            try { href = a.getAttribute('href') || ' '; } catch (e) { href = ' '; }
            var t = 'full';
            if (href.indexOf('track=a') >= 0) { t = 'track-a'; }
            else if (href.indexOf('track=b') >= 0) { t = 'track-b'; }
            else if (href.indexOf('track=c') >= 0) { t = 'track-c'; }
            lsSet('tracks:active', t);
            try { ev.preventDefault(); } catch (e) {}
            var base = ' ';
            try { base = location.pathname || ' '; } catch (e) { base = ' '; }
            var url = base + '?track=' + t + '#m0c';
            try { location.hash = '#m0c'; } catch (e) {}
            try { history.replaceState(null, ' ', url); } catch (e) {}
            applyFilter(t);
            paintCounts();
          });
        } catch (e) {}
      })(nodes[i]);
    }
  }
  function init() {
    var t = parseTrack();
    lsSet('tracks:active', t);
    applyFilter(t);
    wireLinks();
    paintCounts();
  }
  try {
    if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
      document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
        init();
        setTimeout(function () { applyFilter(parseTrack()); wireLinks(); paintCounts(); }, 800);
      });
    } else {
      init();
      setTimeout(function () { applyFilter(parseTrack()); wireLinks(); paintCounts(); }, 800);
    }
  } catch (e) {}
})();
```

### Contract & validator compliance checklist

* New file only (`只改自己负责的文件`); `id/part/num/title/en/minutes/tags` are its own (`m0c/0/00c`), nothing existing renamed.
* Body uses only allowlisted classes (`lead, blk, blk-tip, blk-warn, tbl, small, flow, nd, hi, ar, grid2, card, kv, acc, acc-body, pill, ic, cm`) — no `tag/min/nav/mod` classes, no `<style>`, no inline `style=`, no `<script>`.
* `String.raw` body with no backtick/`${` in prose, code, comments, or runtime JS (concatenation only).
* Math: 3 paired ASCII-only displays, no CJK inside; code fences excluded from math extraction.
* Tables: all header/body column counts equal; every `blk` has `<h4>`; zero quizzes (links to existing `appF/appB` checks instead); `h3` = 5 (≥2).
* Anchors exclusively to verified ids; `?track=` links bypass the `href="#…"` dead-link check by construction.
* Runtime guarded by `typeof document/location` early-return, so `validate.mjs` `vm` load succeeds; browser path defers past `COURSE.boot` via `DOMContentLoaded` + 800ms re-apply (covers `renderNav/renderSections` timing without touching `index.html`).
